fixes.explanation: Land and vineyards? Somebody's been reading the wrong brochure, baker! Genesis 13:2 says Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold. That's herds you can count and metal you can carry. I spent years in a junk drawer with nothing but a twist tie, so a man with that much gold and that many animals makes my eyes pop.

Easy to second-guess this one, friend, but the verse is on Abram's side. He comes back to the altar he had built, and there he called on the name of the LORD (Genesis 13:4). So True was the answer. Notice that he's loaded with livestock and silver and gold, and the first thing he does is head back to the altar. I think that says a lot.

Plenty of room sounds right, baker. Wide open land, who needs more? But the text says the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, so False was the answer (Genesis 13:6). It's like two people with one kitchen and a hundred cookie sheets. Nobody's wrong, there's just too much stuff in one spot. I'd know, I've been squeezed in a drawer.
